sources.sections: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, Chapter 4: multinomial naive Bayes, logistic regression and evaluation. scikit-learn 1.9, Feature extraction, TF-IDF term weighting
sources.verification: Match count denominators, smoothing and L2 scaling. Identical unigram vectors for two opposing labels. Compute bigram probabilities and the first gradient components.

sources.sections: Joulin et al., EACL 2017 §§2–2.2 and Figure 1
sources.verification: Recompute averaging and the output logit on the review. Distinguish rank factorization, n-gram composition, and learned contextual vectors.

sources.sections: Devlin et al., BERT §3 and Appendix A.5, Figure 4b; D2L §16.6.1 and Figure 16.6.1
sources.verification: One [CLS]-associated readout for the whole sequence, optionally pooled; numerical head example and binary vs two-class interpretation.

sources.sections: scikit-learn, Classification of text documents using sparse features, feature effect on original data
sources.verification: Check the authors’ 20 Newsgroups caltech metadata example. Demonstrate distinct precision, recall, and review workloads for two hypothetical thresholds.

figures.modifications: Poppler crop of complete diagram on source PDF page 2. Labels unchanged.

verification.explanation: Read both editions against the source steps. Preserved the classification task and label meaning across bag-of-words, fastText, BERT, and evaluation. Neighbouring NER and T5 changed only their reading navigation and corresponding revision pins.
verification.example: The shared Python block reproduces equal unigram vectors, smoothed weights, distinct bigram probabilities 0.688/0.356, first gradient signs, and the naive Bayes ratio. An independent test recomputes pooling, the contextual head and the threshold tradeoff.
